open_points.subject: external AI provider
open_points.text: Its language model runs at an external AI provider
open_points.question: Which provider or set of providers is inside this trust boundary, and is the provider fixed per deployment, selected per agent session, or variable without Registry knowing it?
options: one named provider
a declared allow-list of providers
any provider chosen outside Registry
open_points.default_guess: Registry does not know the provider; governance records the actual provider used by each agent environment.

open_points.subject: customer erasure
open_points.text: erase a customer's contact data ... keeps only its identity and the fact that it was erased; name, phone, e-mail and language are gone
open_points.question: Does this action also erase the newly stored tax id and legal name, or do those fiscal values survive even though the Customer is said to keep only its identity and erased fact?
options: erase contact and fiscal data
erase contact data but retain fiscal data
provide a separate fiscal-data erasure action
open_points.default_guess: Erase all contact and fiscal data, leaving only customer_ref and the erased fact.

open_points.subject: customer revision workflow
open_points.text: read a customer | owner | name, kind, phone, e-mail, language, tax id and legal name; whether it is restricted, and the date its relationship was marked ended if it is
open_points.question: How does the owner obtain the Customer's current revision required for a stale-safe correction or other Customer change when the customer read and list outputs do not promise to return it?
options: include the revision in read customer
include the revision in both read and list customers
use a separate revision lookup
open_points.default_guess: Return the current revision in every full Customer read.

open_points.subject: archived-project anonymisation
open_points.text: An anonymised project keeps its id, status and artifact pointers and nothing else ... It holds no personal value
open_points.question: What happens when a retained artifact pointer contains a URI, payload_ref or digest that identifies a person or object, which R0-68 says Registry does not inspect and does not refuse?
options: refuse anonymisation and require whole deletion
remove or rewrite offending pointers
accept an owner/governance assertion without Registry checking it
retain the pointers despite the no-personal-value promise
open_points.default_guess: Do not allow the anonymised outcome unless the owner has established that every retained pointer is non-identifying; otherwise delete the project whole.

open_points.subject: register an agent session
open_points.text: the session Registry knows, with no granted project
open_points.question: On registering an already registered session that has grants or an active project, does the output preserve and show its existing access as R0-53's 'returns it unchanged' requires, or reset it to the no-grant state promised here?
options: return the existing session unchanged
reset the existing session
refuse duplicate registration
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing session unchanged, preserving all grants, active project and pending request.

open_points.subject: answer an access request
open_points.text: granting adds the project the owner picks from the catalogue to the session's set (and, if asked, makes it active)
open_points.question: What is the result if the selected project has become unknown, archived, anonymised, deleted, or is already granted before the owner answers?
options: refuse the answer and keep the request pending
clear the request but make no access change
treat an already-granted project as success while refusing unavailable projects
open_points.default_guess: Treat an already-granted active project as an idempotent grant; refuse unavailable projects and leave the request pending.

open_points.subject: answering a replaced access request
open_points.text: a pending request ... replacing the session's earlier pending one ... a request no longer pending refused
open_points.question: How does an owner answer the request they actually viewed rather than a newer request that replaced it between viewing and submitting, when no request identity, request version or expected access version is required?
options: answer by immutable request id
answer against an expected access version
always answer whichever request is currently pending
open_points.default_guess: Require the pending request's identity or version and refuse a stale answer without clearing the newer request.

open_points.subject: access-request outcome
open_points.text: the session reads the outcome in its access
open_points.question: How can the session distinguish a decline from a grant that leaves the set unchanged, such as granting a project already in the set, when access exposes only the set, active project, pending flag and an undefined access version?
options: forbid granting an already-granted project
return an explicit last outcome
define access-version changes so the outcome is inferable
accept that these outcomes are indistinguishable
open_points.default_guess: Forbid answering a request by granting an already-granted project, so clearing the request with no new grant unambiguously means decline.

open_points.subject: session access version
open_points.text: the session's granted project ids, its active project if any, whether it has a pending request, and the access version
open_points.question: What state changes advance the access version, what is its initial value, and is it only informational or also a concurrency precondition for owner actions?
options: advance on every grant, revoke, active-project change and request change
advance only when effective access changes
use it as an optimistic-concurrency precondition
return it only as an informational sequence
open_points.default_guess: Start at 1, advance on every change to grants, active project or pending request, and require the expected version for owner changes that can race.

open_points.subject: migration mapping confirmation
open_points.text: an explicit import whose mapping the owner checks
open_points.question: What action and observable output let the owner inspect the proposed project, customer, object, room and pointer identity mapping before confirming the atomic import?
options: a separate import-preview action followed by confirm
a dry-run mode of the import action followed by the applying call
confirmation without a Registry-produced preview
open_points.default_guess: Provide a non-mutating import preview that shows the complete mapping and conflicts, then confirm that exact preview.

open_points.subject: imported project names
open_points.text: the owner may give each a new display name ... Projects imported under a person's name are renamed ... in the import itself
open_points.question: Is a replacement display name optional for every imported project, or mandatory for a selected project whose legacy name is a person's name, and how is that requirement enforced when no corresponding import failure is declared?
options: require a replacement name for every imported project
require it only for specifically identified person-named imports
leave renaming entirely to the owner without validation
open_points.default_guess: Require a replacement display name for each imported project, while leaving the alias optional.

open_points.subject: project display-name rule
open_points.text: The owner names a project by its object and work, never by a person
open_points.question: Does Registry refuse a create, correction or import whose display name names a person, or is this only a rule on the owner that Registry does not inspect, as explicitly stated for aliases but not for display names?
options: semantic validation and refusal
a writer rule with no Registry check
validation only during the one controlled import
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a writer rule with no semantic Registry check, and state that violating names are accepted but remain personal_data and never reach the agent.
